Logging._efNote: EF Core at Information logs every command it executes, and in production every one of those lines is ingested twice — as a container console line and as an App Insights trace — outside the request sampler. Before this override the readiness probe's three queries every ten seconds were most of the API's log volume. Development keeps the command log (appsettings.Development.json); production has the SQL dependency spans for the same information. (This note sits beside LogLevel rather than inside it: every key under LogLevel is parsed as a level.)

ConnectionStrings._note: Provide DefaultConnection via user secrets in development (dotnet user-secrets), or environment/Key Vault in production. Never commit the real connection string.

Transcription._note: On-demand handwriting transcription (POST /sources/{id}/transcribe). Shares the Loremaster ChatClient and deployment, so cost is priced from Loremaster:ModelPricing. Only the wait is separate: several photographed pages are a much larger prompt than a question, and the caller is a person who would rather wait than be told to retake a good photo.

Loremaster._aiModelNote: AiModel is the Azure OpenAI deployment name, not the model name. Deployment 'nornis-ask' -> model gpt-5.4 (snapshot 2026-03-05; upgraded from gpt-5.4-mini 2026-07-16 for answer quality — also powers Continuity Audit and Retrospective via the shared client). The ModelPricing key MUST match AiModel or cost tracking silently records $0. Rates per 1M tokens (verify against your resource's pricing blade): input $2.50 / output $15.00.

DemoWorlds._note: Feature 20: demo worlds. TemplatePath points at the curated world-export zip (relative paths resolve against the app base directory); empty disables demo creation. PublicAccessEnabled=false is the kill switch that takes all public demo-world views offline (slugs are kept).

Status._note: GET /status is the anonymous ops surface (dependency probes); GET /health stays the deploy-broken signal the availability alert watches. DashboardOrigins lists the origins allowed to fetch /status cross-origin — the status page's home is decided in test-quality phase 2; empty means no CORS, which curl and same-origin callers do not need.
